parts.label: a
parts.technique: Calculating Sxy (sum of products) for bivariate data
parts.reason: Sdw is the sum-of-products statistic used only as a stepping stone to PMCC/regression, both of which involve formula-based calculation excluded by S5.1 ('use of the formula is not required') and used for regression (S2.2 excluded).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Identifying response variable
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly covers explanatory (independent) and response (dependent) variables in bivariate data context; this is a conceptual identification not a regression/correlation calculation.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Calculating PMCC using formula
parts.reason: S5.1 explicit exclusion: 'use of the formula is not required'; here the formula is required using Sdw, Sdd, Sww, so this is exactly the excluded method with no alternative full-marks route shown.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Finding regression line equation
parts.reason: S2.2 explicit exclusion: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Using regression equation for estimate and commenting on reliability
parts.reason: This part only makes sense after using the out-of-spec regression equation from (d); depends entirely on an out-of-spec result.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sum of probabilities equals 1 for discrete distribution
parts.reason: S4.1 covers discrete probability distributions generally; writing the equation that probabilities sum to 1 is basic distribution work, not the excluded mean/variance calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding q using E(X)
parts.reason: Requires calculating E(X) of a general discrete random variable, explicitly excluded by S4.1 ('calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables is excluded').

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Finding p using value of q from part (b)
parts.reason: Uses the value of q obtained via the excluded E(X) calculation in part (b); the part only makes sense after that out-of-spec result.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Finding Var(X) of a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion of calculation of variance of discrete random variables.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Finding E(R) for R = 1/X
parts.reason: Requires E(X)-type calculation (expectation of a function of a discrete random variable) explicitly excluded by S4.1, and depends on p, q values from out-of-spec parts.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Probabilities comparing Sarah's and Rebecca's scores
parts.reason: Depends on values of p and q obtained from the excluded E(X) calculations in earlier parts, so only makes sense after out-of-spec working.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Calculating standard deviation from summary statistics
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly permits calculating standard deviation including from summary statistics such as sum of x^2.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Showing Syy from summary statistics
parts.reason: This is a sum-of-squares calculation analogous to Sxx in S2.3 (used for standard deviation), not a correlation-coefficient or regression-line calculation itself.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Calculating Sxy from summary statistics
parts.reason: Sxy is used solely as a stepping stone to PMCC via formula, which S5.1 explicitly excludes ('use of the formula is not required'); this is precisely that excluded formula-based approach.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Calculating PMCC using the formula
parts.reason: S5.1 explicitly excludes use of the formula for r; only calculator use is permitted, but the mark scheme requires the Sxy/Sxx/Syy formula method here.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Informal reasoning about effect of an added data point on correlation
parts.reason: S2.2 covers informal interpretation of correlation and recognising sections of data affecting correlation strength/sign; this is conceptual reasoning, not a formula calculation, and does not strictly require the out-of-spec numeric r value.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Reading probability from Venn diagram
parts.reason: S3.1/S3.2 cover use of Venn diagrams for probability.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Using independence P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) to find unknown
parts.reason: S3.1 explicitly covers use of independence condition P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Finding remaining probability from total = 1
parts.reason: Basic probability calculation from Venn diagram, covered by S3.1/S3.2.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Conditional probability from Venn diagram
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly covers conditional probability including Venn diagrams and the formula P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B).

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Using probabilities to estimate frequencies in a sample
parts.reason: Application of conditional probabilities calculated in (d) to a sample size, standard S3.2 application.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Histogram bar width/height using frequency density
parts.reason: S2.1 explicitly covers histograms and that area represents frequency.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Linear interpolation for median from grouped data
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers use of linear interpolation for grouped data (percentiles including median).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Estimating mean and standard deviation from grouped data
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculation of mean and standard deviation for grouped/continuous data.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution via calculator.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Critiquing appropriateness of Normal model using mean/median/skew and probability comparison
parts.reason: S4.3 explicitly covers selecting/critiquing appropriateness of a Normal model with reasoning.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Effect of adding a data value on mean and standard deviation
parts.reason: S2.3/S2.4 cover interpretation and drawing inferences about measures of central tendency and variation; this is standard reasoning about summary statistics.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Inverse Normal calculation to find a value given a percentile
parts.reason: S4.2 covers use of Normal distribution including solving for unknowns via calculator (simultaneous equations context implies inverse Normal use too).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Conditional probability using Normal distribution probabilities
parts.reason: S3.2 covers the conditional probability formula P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B) generally, applied here with probabilities from a Normal distribution (S4.2); no statement excludes combining these.
